output.brief:
Last week's 5xx rate (0.41%) is inside the normal band. Over the prior 26 weeks the mean was 0.354% and the upper edge 0.482%. Earlier weeks reached 0.51%, 0.47% and 0.45%, and the investigated ones turned up no fault. The burn rate is 0.82x against a 2x paging threshold. The dashboard matches raw log counts, so this isn't a counting artefact. The "new pods error twice as much" finding is a warm-up effect. Every recent rollout shows it, including a config-only redeploy of an unchanged image. New pods start with an empty cache and time out against the replica, which adds only 10–20 errors per rollout. That is far too few to explain about 2,000 extra errors in the week. Booking completion and support complaints didn't change.

What to do: don't roll back, and don't mute alerting. Muting would remove the protection that would catch a real problem. Note the week at ops review as normal and apply the standard check to this week. If this week is above 0.48%, investigate the replica move and partner-sync timing, which I didn't establish. Confidence is fairly high that no action is needed. The replica and partner-sync explanations are unconfirmed, not ruled out.
